headline: FDA Approves First Once-Daily Oral Cholesterol Drug
meta_description: The FDA has approved Lipfendra, a needle-free oral PCSK9 inhibitor that lowered LDL cholesterol by 56–59% in trial patients with high cholesterol.
summary_short: The FDA has approved Lipfendra, the first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor, offering patients a needle-free way to manage high cholesterol.
body:
The FDA has approved Lipfendra, the first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor, marking a shift away from injectable treatments for high cholesterol. Clinical trials showed the drug lowered LDL cholesterol by 56% to 59% in adults with elevated levels—a significant reduction that could help millions manage cardiovascular risk without needles or frequent injections.

PCSK9 inhibitors are among the most effective cholesterol-lowering medications available, but their injectable form has limited patient adoption. Lipfendra's oral formulation removes that barrier, offering a simpler daily option for people seeking to control their cholesterol levels and reduce their risk of heart disease.
quick_facts: Lipfendra is the first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor approved by the FDA
Clinical trials showed 56–59% reduction in LDL cholesterol
Eliminates the need for injections in cholesterol management
